RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Lawson
Member ID: W261288012
Reference Number: POC-F781755028-57061
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-07
Requested Service/CPT: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (Reference No. POC-F781755028-57061). The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I respectfully disagree and ask that Premera reverse this determination based on the clinical documentation summarized below, which I believe satisfies the medical necessity criteria in Premera's medical policy 7.01.590, "Shoulder Arthroplasty" (Effective Date: April 1, 2026; Last Revised: March 23, 2026).

That policy states that total shoulder arthroplasty "may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met":

"There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following: Degenerative joint disease (DJD), Osteoarthritis (OA), Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), Traumatic arthritis, or Avascular necrosis AND Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following: Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration OR Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration AND Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following: Irregular joint surfaces, Glenoid sclerosis, Glenoid osteophyte changes, Flattened glenoid, Cystic changes in the humeral head, or Joint space narrowing AND Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics, or Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate AND A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: Physical therapy, Activity modification, or Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises"

My clinical record satisfies each of these elements:

1. Diagnosis of degenerative/osteoarthritic joint disease: Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) obtained 2026-06-15 show "complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid," consistent with a diagnosis of glenohumeral osteoarthritis/degenerative joint disease.

2. Disabling pain and functional disability of at least 3 months' duration: I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain unrelieved by rest. As a result, I cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without assistance, and cannot sleep on the affected side. On examination there is glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation is limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation is limited to 10 degrees.

3. Radiographic/imaging evidence within 12 months of the proposed surgery: The 2026-06-15 imaging documents multiple findings enumerated in the policy's list, including glenoid sclerosis, glenoid osteophyte changes, a flattened glenoid, and joint space narrowing.

4. Three months of failed non-operative conservative management: I was treated with NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-28 that produced only 3 weeks of partial relief.

5. Six-week trial of supervised physical measures: I completed 8 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-06-28, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 6-week trial referenced in the policy.

In addition, the policy identifies certain findings that would make total shoulder arthroplasty "not medically necessary," including "Active infection of the joint or active systemic bacteremia," "Active skin infection or open wound within the planned surgical site," "Inadequate bone stock to support implantation of prosthesis," and other exclusionary conditions. None of these exclusions apply to me: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. CT imaging confirms an intact rotator cuff, and there is no documented bone stock deficiency or other contraindication identified in my record.

Because the documented diagnosis, symptom duration, imaging findings, and conservative treatment history each correspond to the specific criteria set out in Premera medical policy 7.01.590, I ask that the plan reverse its determination and approve prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472).

Enclosed with this appeal are the following records supporting this request:
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 18 visits from 2026-05-03 to 2026-06-28
- Medication and injection records, including NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-28
- Shoulder radiographs and CT report dated 2026-06-15
- Office examination notes documenting range-of-motion findings and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from [Dr. Marchetti / treating surgeon], MD, Orthopedic Surgery

If any additional documentation is needed to complete this review, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my surgeon's office at [practice name, phone number]. I understand this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice (by 2027-02-03), and I am submitting it well within that window.

I also request, pursuant to my appeal rights, a copy of the complete medical policy and any clinical review criteria, guidelines, or internal notes relied upon by the reviewer in issuing this denial, including confirmation of the specific policy version applied to my claim.

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this matter.

Sincerely,

Taylor Lawson
Member ID: W261288012
[Signature]
[Date]

cc: [Dr. Marchetti / treating surgeon's office], [Fax/Address]

Note to patient: The quoted policy language above was retrieved directly from Premera's published Medical Policy 7.01.590, "Shoulder Arthroplasty" (individual/ACA plan version). All other statements in this letter are arguments framed in my own words, not quotations from the plan. Before sending, please confirm the correct current mailing/fax address for member appeals by calling the Customer Service number on the back of your member ID card, since Premera's published materials list more than one appeals address depending on plan type.
